milestone: Track 2 exception isolation — duplicate groups resolved in place
problem: The Track 2 exception surface isolated anomalies correctly and then stopped at diagnosis. It answered 'what is wrong' and left 'what do I do about it' to the operator. The exact-duplicate exception card recommended 'Decide this source individually in the review queue' — sending the operator to find a record the system already held in memory, to re-derive a canonical-copy judgement the system could already make from recorded quality signals, and to re-type a rationale the system could already compose. The isolation was constitutionally correct and operationally incomplete: an exception that never terminates in an executable act converts a governance control into an obstruction.
observedFailure: The duplicate exception card's recommendedAction read 'Decide this source individually in the review queue' — a navigation instruction, not an act.
Both duplicate members were already loaded in the surface's own state, yet the operator was asked to locate them elsewhere.
The canonical-copy choice was presented as requiring human judgement even where artifact hash, extraction status, metadata completeness and existing lineage clearly separated the two copies.
No rationale was pre-composed, so a steward who accepted the obvious treatment still had to author the justification from a blank field.
All manual-review exceptions carried the same amber weight, so a group needing one confirmation looked as burdensome as one needing genuine editorial judgement.
The consequence of resolving a group — which record survives, whether anything is deleted, whether the freeze is affected — was nowhere stated before the act.
rootCauses: The exception model was designed around ISOLATION (which record is affected, what does it block) and never around RESOLUTION (what is the smallest safe act that clears it).
IsolationException carries `recommendedAction` as free prose, which permitted a navigation instruction to satisfy the type while offering no act.

The governed treatment already existed — `mark_duplicate` with `duplicateOfSourceId` in applyCandidateReviewDecision — but nothing derived WHICH source should be canonical, so the surface could not offer it.
Quality signals sufficient to rank two copies of identical bytes were already recorded on every row and were never read for this purpose.

Exceptions were classified by CAUSE (duplicate, unreadable, provenance) but never by whether human judgement was actually required, so a mechanical decision and an editorial one were presented identically.
resolution: Added services/corpusScout/duplicateResolution.ts: derives a recommended canonical copy from quality signals that already exist on the row, explains the derivation signal by signal, states the consequence before the act, and pre-composes an editable rationale.

Split exceptions into 'recommended-resolution-available' and 'genuine-judgment-required'. Only the second warrants deeper inspection; equal scores yield the second rather than a coin-flip presented as a derivation.

Added POST /api/corpus-scout/candidates/resolve-duplicates performing the whole governed treatment in one step, by looping the EXISTING single-source applier once per alias — no new write path, and bulk-review's deliberate refusal of mark_duplicate is honoured rather than relaxed.
Both records are always preserved: mark_duplicate is an update that records duplicateOfSourceId, never a delete. A canary asserts no code path in the resolution chain deletes a candidate source.

Added a dry run in the operator's own shape (duplicate records / canonical retained / aliases excluded / records deleted / unrelated affected / freeze impact) computed from the same plans the execution uses, so preview and act cannot disagree.

The batch act operates only on groups carrying a deterministic recommendation; ambiguous groups are listed in `skipped` by name rather than silently omitted, so a group that needs judgement can never look resolved.
Receipts ride the existing cohortAuthorization machinery, carrying the authorizing steward and the affected cohort hash.
rejectedApproaches: Improving the wording of the recommendedAction string. The defect was not that the instruction was unclear but that it was an instruction at all; a better-worded scavenger hunt is still a scavenger hunt.
Auto-resolving duplicate groups without confirmation. The ruling asks for the smallest safe act to be OFFERED, not performed unilaterally — admission and exclusion remain steward acts.

Picking a canonical copy by first-seen or lowest id when signals tie. That presents an arbitrary preference as a derivation; the honest answer is that the system cannot tell, which is exactly the 'genuine judgment required' class.

Relaxing bulk-review's refusal of mark_duplicate so the batch act could reuse it. That refusal exists because the alias target is a per-source fact; looping the single-source applier honours it instead.
Deleting the duplicate row. Simpler and irreversible: it destroys the provenance record of an acquisition that really happened, and the ruling requires both records preserved.
Adding a `blocking` boolean to distinguish burdensome exceptions. The distinction needed is whether JUDGEMENT is required, which is a property of the evidence, not of severity.
